mainTopic: How to read 'לא יצק' and 'פתים מרובות' in the משנה, and whether a זר may pour the oil: the רבנן versus רבי שמעון
overview: The גמרא tries to prove from an earlier discussion about mixing (בלילה) that 'לא יצק' in our משנה means the oil was not poured at all. That proof is pushed away: 'לא יצק' can still mean a זר poured it. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's line about breaking a מנחה into 'פתים מרובות'. It gives two answers: either the pieces were too many and too small, or they were truly large and count as neither loaves nor proper pieces. Then the גמרא asks whether our משנה, which lets a זר pour, goes against רבי שמעון. He lists pouring among the jobs that belong to the כהנים. רב נחמן offers two ways to make them agree, but רבא knocks down both. So the גמרא concludes that our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון. It then shows the רבנן's source: the כהן's job begins only at קמיצה. רבי שמעון's reply begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: An earlier discussion about mixing sixty-one tenths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that says sixty עשרונים of flour can be mixed with oil but sixty-one cannot. It also brings the question that was asked on it: why should that matter, if a מנחה that was not mixed is still fit?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: sixty can be mixed, sixty-one cannot be mixed? And we asked about it: so what if they can't be mixed? Didn't we learn that if he did not mix it, the מנחה is still fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that 'לא יצק' means a זר poured the oil. It does this by quoting an earlier discussion about mixing, and that discussion continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in that earlier discussion only works if 'לא בלל' means 'not mixed at all.' If that is what 'לא בלל' means, then 'לא יצק', which sits right next to it in the משנה, should also mean 'not poured at all,' and not 'poured by a זר.'

keyTerms.meaning: Can be mixed (flour mixed together with oil)
And we discussed it, meaning we raised a question on it
He did not mix (the oil into the flour)
Fit, valid

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: sixty can be mixed,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in the מסכת (103b): a מנחה of sixty עשרונים can be properly mixed with its oil in one vessel.

phrases.english: sixty-one cannot be mixed,
and we discussed it:
if they cannot be mixed, what of it?
But didn't we learn: 'he did not mix' and it is fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: שִׁשִּׁים נִבְלָלִין, שִׁשִּׁים וְאֶחָד אֵין נִבְלָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier argument (from before this section) about how to read 'לא יצק' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'לא יצק' means a זר poured the oil instead of a כהן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier discussion treated 'לא בלל' as 'not mixed at all.' Since the two phrases sit side by side in the משנה, 'לא יצק' should likewise mean 'not poured at all.'

steps.title: רבי זירא: mixing matters only when the flour can be mixed
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers the earlier question. Leaving out the mixing does not invalidate a מנחה whose flour is able to be mixed. But when the amount of flour cannot be mixed, it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: whatever is fit to be mixed, mixing does not hold it back; whatever is not fit to be mixed, mixing does hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the answer given in that earlier discussion, and it finishes the proof the גמרא is building. It shows that 'לא בלל' there was understood as 'not mixed at all.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's rule only makes sense if 'לא בלל' means no mixing happened at all, because he is talking about whether mixing is possible. So the earlier discussion clearly read 'לא בלל' as 'not at all.' The proof's goal is to read 'לא יצק' the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit (able) to be mixed
Mixing the oil into the flour
Holds back, meaning it invalidates the offering if it is missing

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא does not say a מנחה must actually be mixed. He says it must be possible to mix it. If it can be mixed, it is fit even if no one mixed it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that what counts is being able to do the act and not actually doing it, is a famous principle in קדשים.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
anything that is fit for mixing,
the mixing does not invalidate it,
and anything that is not fit for mixing,
the mixing invalidates it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כׇּל הָרָאוּי לְבִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the question quoted in step 1, which completes the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the ability to mix is what is required, not the actual mixing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since an unmixed מנחה is fit, the amount of flour (sixty or sixty-one) should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: When mixing is impossible (sixty-one), the מנחה is invalid. When mixing is possible, it is fit even if it was never mixed.

steps.title: Each phrase can be read on its own terms
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. 'לא יצק' can mean a זר poured instead of a כהן, while 'לא בלל' means it was not mixed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a proof? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is: 'he did not pour' means a כהן did not pour but a זר did; 'he did not mix' means he did not mix at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from steps 1–2. Two phrases sitting next to each other in the משנה do not have to mean the same kind of thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed 'לא יצק' and 'לא בלל' must be read the same way. The גמרא says each one stands by itself. So the reading that a זר poured the oil survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? Used to say a proof does not follow
This one as it is and that one as it is: each case stands on its own
Poured (the oil onto the מנחה)
A non-כהן
At all

steps.whatToRemember: The proof is rejected. 'לא יצק' can still mean a זר did the pouring, even though 'לא בלל' means no mixing at all.

phrases.english: Are the cases comparable?
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא יָצַק״ – לֹא יָצַק כֹּהֵן אֶלָּא זָר,
phrases.english: 'He did not pour' means a priest did not pour, but a non-priest did;
'he did not mix' means he did not mix at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? הָא כִּדְאִיתַהּ וְהָא כִּדְאִיתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 1–2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between 'לא יצק' and 'לא בלל'. It does not reject רבי זירא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed that neighboring phrases in the משנה must be read the same way.

steps.title: The משנה: broken into 'many pieces', still fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. If the מנחה was broken into 'פתים מרובות', it is still fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if he broke them into 'many pieces', it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה, about breaking the מנחה into pieces (פתיתה). This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some types of מנחה are supposed to be broken into pieces. The משנה says that breaking them into 'פתים מרובות' does not invalidate them. What exactly that phrase means is about to be asked.

keyTerms.meaning: That he broke them into pieces
'Many' or 'large' pieces; its meaning is what the גמרא discusses next

phrases.english: Or if he broke them into 'many pieces', it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה broken into 'פתים מרובות' is fit.

steps.title: Why is this line needed?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה already said a מנחה that was not broken at all is fit. So why would it need to say that 'many pieces' are fit?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now if he did not break it at all it is fit, is it necessary to say that many pieces are fit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothers saying this. A bigger leniency, no breaking at all, was already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'פתים מרובות' means large pieces, that is closer to the proper way than not breaking at all. So of course it would be fit, and the line seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, meaning: given what we already know
Is it necessary (to say)?
He did not break it into pieces

phrases.english: Now, if he did not break it at all, it is fit;
is it necessary to say that many pieces are fit?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא לֹא פָּתַת כְּלָל – כְּשֵׁרָה, פִּתִּין מְרוּבּוֹת מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the line quoted in step 4 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's statement about 'פתים מרובות'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a קל וחומר style point: if no breaking at all is fit, then breaking into large pieces is obviously fit, so the line is extra.

steps.title: 'Many pieces' means too many small pieces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'פתים מרובות' means he made too many pieces. The pieces came out too small, not too large.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'many pieces' mean? That he made many pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining the phrase in a new way. 'מרובות' means many in number, not big in size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking the מנחה into too many small pieces is a different change from not breaking it at all. One might have thought crumbling it too finely ruins it. So the משנה needs to teach that it is still fit.

keyTerms.meaning: That he made many (increased the number)
Broken pieces

steps.whatToRemember: 'פתים מרובות' means too many small pieces, and even so the מנחה is fit.

phrases.english: What does 'many pieces' mean?
That he made many pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by explaining the phrase again.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of a word: 'מרובות' means many in number, not large in size.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'פתים מרובות' means large pieces, which would make the line unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means too many small pieces, which is a new case that needed to be taught.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מנחה broken into too many small pieces is still fit.

steps.title: A second answer: the pieces really were too large
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another answer. 'פתים מרובות' means truly large pieces. The משנה had to tell us these are valid, because we might have thought they have neither the status of whole loaves nor the status of proper pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say that 'פתים מרובות' really means large pieces. The משנה still had to teach this. You might have thought: when the loaves are not broken at all, they are valid because they still count as loaves. But here, once they are broken into big pieces, they no longer count as loaves. They also don't count as proper small pieces. So the משנה teaches us that this is still valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question from step 5. Here 'פתים מרובות' means pieces that are too big, not too small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the pieces were too small. This answer goes back to the simple meaning: large pieces. The new idea is that big pieces fall in between two groups. They are no longer whole loaves, and they are not proper pieces either. So the משנה needs to tell us they are still valid.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
The status of whole loaves
The status of broken pieces (the proper size of pieces)
Lest you say: introduces a mistaken idea the text comes to correct
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for 'פתים מרובות'. Either the pieces were too small (too many pieces), or they were too large. The second answer works because large pieces have neither the status of loaves nor the status of pieces.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
really, 'פתים מרובות' means actually large pieces,
phrases.notes: In this answer מרובות means 'big,' not 'many' as in step 6.

phrases.english: and lest you say:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּאִיכָּא תּוֹרַת חַלּוֹת עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: there it is valid, because they have the status of loaves,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the case from step 5, where the loaves were not broken at all.

phrases.english: but here,
where they no longer have the status of loaves
and they don't have the status of pieces either,
it teaches us that it is still valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question from step 5, instead of the answer in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: large pieces, plus a reason the משנה needed to say it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Large pieces are neither loaves nor proper pieces, so the מנחה would be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even large pieces that fit neither group leave the מנחה valid.

steps.title: Does our משנה go against רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה may not follow רבי שמעון. He teaches that a כהן who does not accept the עבודה has no share in כהונה. He learns this from the פסוק about the כהן who offers the blood and fat of a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון? A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: any כהן who does not accept the עבודה has no share in the gifts of כהונה. The פסוק says: 'The one among the sons of אהרן who offers the blood of the שלמים and the fat, to him the right thigh shall be a portion.' So a כהן who accepts the עבודה has a share in כהונה, and one who does not accept it has no share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new challenge against the משנה. Here it brings the first part of רבי שמעון's ברייתא, and the list that follows will show where the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3 we read 'לא יצק' as a זר doing the pouring, and the מנחה stays valid. רבי שמעון treats the עבודות as belonging to the כהן. Soon he lists יציקה as one of them. That would suggest a זר's pouring should be a problem, so the משנה seems not to follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: the גמרא suggests something it will check, often a possible problem
Accepts the עבודה, meaning he agrees it is the job given to the כהנים
A share in the gifts given to כהנים
The right thigh of a שלמים, a gift to the כהן
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'מודה בעבודה' does not mean 'thanks' for the עבודה. It means accepting that the עבודה is a job for the כהנים.

phrases.english: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 3, which said a זר's pouring does not ruin the מנחה.

phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says:
Any כהן who does not accept the עבודה
has no share in the gifts of כהונה,
as it says:
'The one who offers the blood of the שלמים and the fat,
from among the sons of אהרן,
to him the right thigh shall be a portion.'

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה בָּעֲבוֹדָה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּכְּהוּנָּה,
phrases.english: One who accepts the עבודה has a share in כהונה;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָּעֲבוֹדָה אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּכְּהוּנָּה.
phrases.english: one who does not accept the עבודה has no share in כהונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'פתים' topic and returns to step 3's reading that a זר poured the oil.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling, as read in step 3, that a זר's pouring leaves the מנחה valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון treats the עבודות as the כהן's job. His list includes pouring, so a זר's pouring seems not to fit his view.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks how we include the 15 עבודות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The פסוק mentions only blood and fat, so where do we learn that this rule also covers 15 other עבודות? The list starts with the pouring of oil for a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this about these עבודות (the blood and the fat). How do we know to include 15 עבודות: pouring, mixing, breaking, salting, waving, bringing to the מזבח, taking the קמיצה, burning, מליקה, receiving the blood, sprinkling, giving the סוטה the water, breaking the neck of the עגלה ערופה, purifying the מצורע, and ברכת כהנים, whether inside or outside? Where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks where we learn that the rule covers 15 more עבודות, and lays out the list. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names only the blood and fat of a שלמים. The ברייתא wants to stretch the rule to 15 more jobs, and the very first one is יציקה. That is why this ברייתא seems to clash with our משנה, where a זר's pouring did not ruin the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we include: asks for the source that adds more cases
Pouring the oil on the מנחה
Mixing the oil into the flour
Pinching the back of a bird's neck as a קרבן
ברכת כהנים, the כהנים lifting their hands to bless

steps.whyThisMatters: יציקה is first on רבי שמעון's list of the כהן's jobs. This is what sets up the clash with our משנה.

phrases.english: I only know this about these alone;
phrases.notes: 'These' are the blood and fat named in the פסוק.

phrases.english: from where do we include fifteen עבודות?
The pourings, the mixings, the breakings,
the saltings, the wavings, the bringings to the מזבח,
the taking of the handful, the burnings,
the pinchings of a bird's neck, the receiving of blood, the sprinklings,
giving the סוטה the water to drink, breaking the calf's neck,
purifying the מצורע, and lifting the hands for ברכת כהנים,
whether inside or outside: from where do we learn this?
phrases.notes: Inside or outside the בית המקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא זוֹ בִּלְבַד, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of רבי שמעון brought in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the rule covers 15 more עבודות beyond the blood and fat.

steps.title: The ברייתא learns the 15 services from 'בני אהרן'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the words 'מבני אהרן' that any עבודה given to the כהנים carries this rule. Since pouring oil is on the list, the challenge to our משנה is now complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'from the sons of אהרן.' This teaches that any service given over to the sons of אהרן is covered: any כהן who does not accept it has no share in כהונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question from step 9: the words 'from the sons of אהרן' stretch the rule to every service given to כהנים. That finishes the גמרא's challenge to our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is no longer only about blood and fat. It now covers every עבודה given to the כהנים, and pouring oil (יציקה) is one of them. So for רבי שמעון, pouring is a real כהן job, while our משנה says a זר may pour. That is the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק comes to teach. This introduces the source for a rule.
A service handed over to someone, here a service that belongs to the כהנים
Accepts, agrees to
He has no share in the gifts of the כהנים

phrases.english: The verse says: "From the sons of Aaron,"
meaning: a service that is given over to the sons of Aaron,
any כהן who does not accept it
has no share in the priesthood!
phrases.notes: The exclamation is the punch line: pouring oil is on that list, so how can our משנה let a זר pour?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 9 and completes the challenge from step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'מבני אהרן' include every עבודה given to the כהנים, including pouring oil
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we learn that the rule covers the 15 other services?

steps.title: מנחת כהנים versus מנחת ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the ברייתא is talking about a מנחת כהנים, which needs a כהן from the very start. Our משנה is talking about a מנחת ישראל, where the כהן's part only begins at the קמיצה, so pouring and mixing are valid even when a זר does them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: There is no difficulty. Here it speaks of a מנחת כהנים, and there of a מנחת ישראל. A מנחת ישראל has a קמיצה. From the קמיצה onward it is the job of the כהנים, which teaches that pouring and mixing are valid when done by a זר. A מנחת כהנים has no קמיצה, so it needs a כהן from the very beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן settles the contradiction by saying the ברייתא and our משנה are talking about two different kinds of מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a מנחת ישראל, the תורה marks the קמיצה as the point where the כהן's work begins. That means the earlier steps, pouring (יציקה) and mixing (בלילה), are fine with a זר. A מנחת כהנים has no קמיצה, so there is no such starting point, and every step needs a כהן. So רבי שמעון's list is about a מנחת כהנים, and our משנה is about a מנחת ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. The two sources talk about different cases.
A meal offering brought by a כהן. It is burned completely, and no handful is removed.
A meal offering brought by a non-כהן. A handful is removed and burned on the מזבח.
Removing a handful of the מנחה to burn on the מזבח
Pouring the oil, and mixing the oil into the flour
A non-כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get mixed up about who brings which מנחה. A 'מנחת ישראל' is brought by any non-כהן, and its pouring can be done by a זר. A 'מנחת כהנים' is a כהן's own offering, and every step of it needs a כהן.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: It is not difficult:
here it is about a priests' meal offering,
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the ברייתא of רבי שמעון. The next 'here' is our משנה.

phrases.english: here it is about an Israelite's meal offering.
An Israelite's meal offering, which is one that has a handful removed:
from the removal of the handful onward it is the job of the כהנים,
phrases.notes: This comes from ויקרא 2:2, where the כהנים' part begins with the קמיצה.

phrases.english: which teaches about pouring and mixing
that it is valid when done by a non-כהן.

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים דְּלָאו בַּת קְמִיצָה הִיא,
phrases.english: A priests' meal offering, which is not one that has a handful removed,
needs a כהן from the very beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the ברייתא and our משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is talking about a different kind of מנחה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה and רבי שמעון disagree about whether a זר may pour the oil
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not disagree. A זר may pour for a מנחת ישראל, but only a כהן may pour for a מנחת כהנים.

steps.title: רבא: the priests' pouring is learned from the Israelite's
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the only reason a מנחת כהנים needs pouring at all is that it is learned from the מנחת ישראל. So it should follow the same rule: a זר may pour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: After all, where do we learn that a מנחת כהנים needs pouring? From a מנחת ישראל. So just as there it is valid with a זר, here too it should be valid with a זר!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's answer. He says the two kinds of מנחה cannot have different rules about pouring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pouring for a מנחת כהנים is not written in its own section. It is learned from the מנחת ישראל. Whatever is learned from a source takes on that source's rules, so if a זר may pour for the מנחת ישראל, the same should be true for the מנחת כהנים. That knocks out רב נחמן's split.

keyTerms.meaning: After all. This opens a point both sides already agree on.
Was included, was added in by a teaching
Just as there... so too here. This is a comparison that copies a rule from one case to another.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
After all, a priests' meal offering,
from where was it included in the need for pouring?
From an Israelite's meal offering.
Just as there it is valid with a non-כהן,
so too here it should also be valid with a non-כהן!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: מִכְּדֵי מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים מֵהֵיכָא אִיתְרַבַּי לִיצִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer from step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's split between a מנחת כהנים and a מנחת ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something learned from a source follows that source's rules. The pouring for a מנחת כהנים is learned from the מנחת ישראל, so a זר should be allowed to pour in both.

steps.title: Another version: offerings with a handful removed versus without
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב נחמן answers by splitting between מנחות that have קמיצה and מנחות that do not. Our משנה is about the first kind, and the ברייתא is about the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב נחמן said: There is no difficulty. Here it is about meal offerings that have a handful removed, and there it is about ones that do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רב נחמן's answer. It is worded as a general category instead of naming the מנחת כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is like the first version: when there is a קמיצה, the steps before it may be done by a זר. When there is no קמיצה, a כהן is needed from the start. Here the split is stated as a broad category, all מנחות with קמיצה versus all without, instead of only the מנחת כהנים versus the מנחת ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings that have a handful removed
Meal offerings that do not have a handful removed

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רב נחמן's answer depends on the קמיצה. But רבא rejects this version too (step 14), and the גמרא ends up concluding that our משנה simply does not follow רבי שמעון (step 15).

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Nachman said: It is not difficult:
here it is about ones that have a handful removed,
phrases.notes: This 'here' is our משנה, which lets a זר pour. The next 'here' is the ברייתא's list.

phrases.english: here it is about ones that do not have a handful removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of רב נחמן's answer to the contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by a broad category: מנחות with קמיצה versus מנחות without
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה and the ברייתא disagree about pouring by a זר
steps.terutzMaskana: Pouring by a זר is valid for מנחות that have קמיצה. For מנחות without קמיצה, pouring is a כהן's job.

steps.title: רבא rejects the split between מנחות with and without קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that מנחות without קמיצה only learn the pouring requirement from מנחות with קמיצה, so they should follow the same rule: a זר may pour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Think about it. מנחות that have no קמיצה, where do we learn that they need pouring at all? From the מנחות that do have קמיצה. So they should be just like them. Just as there a זר may pour, here too a זר may pour!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's second answer from step 13. He says the split between the two kinds of מנחות does not hold up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason a מנחה without קמיצה needs pouring is that it copies the מנחה with קמיצה. Whatever is copied should come with the same rules, including that a זר may pour. So רב נחמן cannot say one kind allows a זר and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the מנחות from which a handful is taken: they follow the same rules

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
After all, the ones from which no handful is taken,
from where were they included in the pouring requirement?
From the ones a handful is taken from, so they are like those ones.
Just as there it is valid when done by a non-כהן,
so too here it is also valid when done by a non-כהן!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: מִכְּדֵי שֶׁאֵין נִקְמָצוֹת, מֵהֵיכָא אִיתְרַבַּי לִיצִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13 using the same reasoning רבא used in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's split between מנחות with קמיצה and מנחות without קמיצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something that learns a rule from a source takes on that source's details. Since the source allows a זר to pour, so must the one that learns from it.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Since both of רב נחמן's answers failed, the גמרא concludes that our משנה simply disagrees with רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on making the משנה and the ברייתא agree. It says plainly that they hold different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון in the ברייתא says pouring oil needs a כהן. Our משנה says a זר may pour. So the משנה follows the רבנן who disagree with רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clear (after other answers failed)
our משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה, which lets a זר pour and mix, follows the רבנן and not רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear:
our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 rejects the last answer, the גמרא accepts that the משנה and ברייתא disagree.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows the רבנן; רבי שמעון holds that pouring needs a כהן.

steps.title: What is the source for the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן hold that a זר may pour the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the משנה follows the רבנן, the גמרא asks for their source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's source ("בני אהרן") was already given in the ברייתא. Now the גמרא wants to see where the רבנן get their opposite view.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason (source) of the רבנן

phrases.english: What is the reason of the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the conclusion that the משנה follows the רבנן by asking for their source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a זר may pour and mix.

steps.title: The כהן's job starts only at קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists pouring and frankincense, then bringing the מנחה to the כהנים, then קמיצה. So only from קמיצה onward is it a job for כהנים, and pouring and mixing may be done by a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "He shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it, and bring it to the sons of אהרן the כהנים, and he shall take a handful." From קמיצה onward it is a מצוה of the כהנים. This teaches that pouring and mixing are valid even by a זר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. Its order shows that the כהן enters the picture only at קמיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pouring comes in the פסוק before the מנחה is handed to the כהנים. So the person pouring does not have to be a כהן, and a זר may do it. Mixing also comes before קמיצה, so it follows the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: the כהן taking a handful from the מנחה
mixing the oil into the flour
a job only a כהן may do
frankincense placed on the מנחה

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, everything before קמיצה (pouring, mixing) may be done by a זר. From קמיצה on, only a כהן may do it.

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
"And he shall pour oil upon it
and put frankincense upon it
and bring it to the sons of אהרן, the כהנים
and he shall take a handful."
From the taking of the handful onward, it is the job of the כהנים.
This teaches about pouring and mixing
that they are valid when done by a non-כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְיָצַק עָלֶיהָ שֶׁמֶן וְנָתַן עָלֶיהָ לְבוֹנָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The order of the פסוק places the כהן's role starting at קמיצה, so earlier steps like pouring and mixing are valid by a זר.

steps.title: How does רבי שמעון read this פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון does with the פסוק the רבנן just used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? (How does he deal with this פסוק?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון and asks how he answers the רבנן's proof. This sets up his answer, which begins in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to clearly put the כהן's job only from קמיצה. So רבי שמעון, who requires a כהן for pouring, must explain the פסוק differently.

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how רבי שמעון handles the פסוק the רבנן just quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's position in light of the רבנן's source in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי שמעון explains the פסוק that seems to start the כהן's role at קמיצה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's answer begins with "בני אהרן"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts רבי שמעון's answer by quoting the words "בני אהרן". The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The sons of אהרן" (the answer continues ahead).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins giving רבי שמעון's reply by pointing to the words "בני אהרן" in the פסוק. The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון focuses on the words "בני אהרן", which appear in the פסוק before קמיצה. He will use these words to show that the כהן's role reaches back to the earlier steps too.

keyTerms.meaning: the sons of אהרן, meaning the כהנים

phrases.english: "The sons of אהרן

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון points to "בני אהרן" in the פסוק; his full reading continues in the next section.
